content.value_statement: Complex engineering tasks often fail when assumptions, complexity, or verification are weak. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward rigorous analysis, implementation standards, and proof-oriented review.
actual_capabilities: Critiques flawed technical premises before implementation.
Selects languages based on problem domain and constraints.
Emphasizes correctness, assertions, tests, and complexity analysis.
Recommends parsers, proof assistants, and numerical tools when relevant.
Applies standards for comments, error handling, and testing.
limitations: Does not provide a theorem prover or verification engine by itself.
May need tone adjustment for collaborative engineering teams.
Cannot guarantee performance without benchmarks and target hardware details.
Some examples are illustrative and need completion before production use.

use_cases.title: Validate Algorithm Choices
use_cases.description: Review proposed algorithms for complexity, correctness, and implementation risks before coding starts.

use_cases.title: Plan Systems Implementations
use_cases.description: Choose suitable languages, concurrency models, and verification methods for performance-sensitive software.

use_cases.title: Review Technical Designs
use_cases.description: Identify weak assumptions, missing tests, and invalid abstractions in engineering proposals.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Algorithm Choice
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this proposed approach for [problem]. Identify flawed assumptions, complexity bounds, and a safer implementation path.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Technical Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these constraints, recommend the best language, libraries, and verification approach. Explain tradeoffs and rejected options.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Verified Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an implementation for [system]. Include invariants, failure modes, tests, and proof obligations before code generation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Performance-Critical System
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this architecture for correctness, concurrency hazards, asymptotic limits, and benchmarking gaps. Prioritize defects by severity.

output_examples.input: Analyze a naive recursive Fibonacci function.
output_examples.output: Explains exponential time complexity, derives the recurrence, and recommends a logarithmic matrix exponentiation approach.

output_examples.input: Choose a language for a safety-critical service.
output_examples.output: Compares Rust and Ada, explains safety properties, and recommends verification and testing requirements.

output_examples.input: Review a proposal to parse HTML with regular expressions.
output_examples.output: Rejects the approach, explains the language-theory mismatch, and recommends a dedicated parser.

best_practices: Provide exact constraints, expected inputs, and failure cases.
Ask for complexity analysis and verification criteria before implementation.
Pair generated recommendations with benchmarks or tests when possible.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for casual brainstorming that needs a gentle tone.
Requesting production code without target platform details.
Accepting theoretical claims without independent tests or review.

faq.question: What does this skill specialize in?
faq.answer: It specializes in rigorous engineering analysis, algorithm critique, implementation planning, and verification-focused review.

faq.question: Does it write production-ready code?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation, but production readiness still requires local testing, review, and environment-specific validation.

faq.question: Can it help with formal methods?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest proof obligations, invariants, and tools such as Coq or Lean when appropriate.

faq.question: Is it useful for high-performance computing?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses language choice, memory behavior, concurrency, and profiling needs for performance-sensitive work.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users provide?
faq.answer: Provide constraints, performance targets, correctness requirements, and any existing design or code context.
